solver: yices (default); z3 cross-checked; bitwuzla unavailable (download blocked, offline)
targets: claim() payment math (src L494-498): claimerPayment = totalNormalizedYield * (10000 - discountRate) / 10000 ; actualPayment = _denormalizeAmount(claimerPayment, rewardToken)
methodology: Two engines. (A) Standalone re-implementation of _normalizeAmount/_denormalizeAmount copied VERBATIM (identical operator order, types, checked 0.8.20 arithmetic) so Halmos can reason over the math with fully-symbolic (amount, decimals, rate, discount) free of the contract's external calls/loops/storage. (B) A subclass harness (SYAHarness) exposing the REAL internal functions, configured through the real setTokenConfig. Equivalence between (A) and the real bytecode is PROVEN (check_implMatchesRealCode_* PASS), so the standalone proofs/counterexamples transfer to the deployed contract. Halmos auto-symbolizes test-function parameters; vm.assume constrains decimals<=18, discount<=10000, rate to realistic ranges.
note_on_failed: All 4 [FAIL] results are EXPECTED refutations: each asserts 'payment > 0' which Halmos refutes with a concrete counterexample, thereby PROVING the zero-payment hazard is reachable. They are not test-harness errors.
note_on_timeout: All 8 [TIMEOUT] results involve a 256-bit multiply-then-divide (x*scale then /scale, or symbolic-rate (x*rate)/1e18). This is a known SMT (yices/z3) weakness on bitvector udiv of a product, NOT a contract defect. The security-relevant direction (no over-charge: normalize(denormalize(y)) <= y) WAS discharged (check_noOvercharge_dec6_rate1_bounded PASS). bitwuzla, which handles bv-division better, could not be used (offline, download blocked).

findings.result: FAIL (refuted: payment can be 0 while yield > 0)
findings.description: Symbolic execution proves actualPayment floors to exactly 0 while a strictly positive amount of yield is skimmed and delivered to the claimer. Confirmed on BOTH the standalone math and the REAL deployed _denormalizeAmount bytecode (check_realCode_denormNonZero_dec6). For a reward token with normalizedExchangeRate == 1e18 and decimals d < 18, _denormalizeAmount divides the 18-dec discounted amount by 10**(18-d); any discounted value below 10**(18-d) becomes 0.

counterexample.result: claimer pays 0 reward token yet receives the underlying yield

findings.proof: Halmos counterexample (yices); reproduced on real bytecode via SYAHarness.exposedDenormalize.

findings.description: Halmos PROVES the precise zero-payment region (no counterexample for either complementary half). For a reward token with normalizedExchangeRate == 1e18 and decimals d < 18: actualPayment == 0  if-and-only-if  claimerPayment < 10**(18 - d), where claimerPayment = floor(totalNormalizedYield * (10000 - discountRate) / 10000). For USDC (d=6) the threshold is 10**12 wei of 18-dec value (= $0.000001 of discounted yield). The discount WIDENS the zero-region by a factor of 10000/(10000 - discountRate).
findings.mostAcuteTrigger: An 18-decimal strategy token (DAI/DOLA/sDAI-style) delivers normalize(x,18dec)=x (no upscaling), so totalNormalizedYield can be as low as a few wei. Against a 6-dec reward token (USDC) this falls below the 1e12 floor, so dust-to-small per-claim surplus is skimmed for zero payment. minRewardTokenSupplied defaults to 0 (guard disabled), so nothing stops a zero-payment claim.
findings.proof: Halmos [PASS] on both check_boundary_aboveThreshold_dec6 and check_boundary_belowThreshold_dec6.

findings.result: PARTIAL-PROOF: no over-charge proven for 6-dec, 1:1 rate, y<1e15; symbolic-rate variants inconclusive (solver timeout)
findings.description: Property normalize(denormalize(y)) <= y (the reward tokens actually charged re-normalize to no MORE than what was owed) is PROVEN for a 6-dec reward token at 1:1 rate over the bounded domain (PASS, 8.7s). No counterexample to over-charge was found anywhere. _denormalizeAmount only ever rounds DOWN (floor), so it cannot over-produce relative to exact arithmetic. The SLITHER-001 divide-before-multiply pattern lives exclusively in the decimals > 18 branch of _denormalizeAmount (src L635-636), which is DEAD CODE: setTokenConfig reverts InvalidDecimals for decimals > 18, so no configured token can reach it. The symbolic-rate variants (check_noOvercharge_dec6/8/18) are INCONCLUSIVE (timeout) due to the nonlinear (y*1e18)/rate bitvector division, not due to any violation.

proofs.property: Standalone normImpl == real _normalizeAmount bytecode for dec6 over symbolic (amount, rate). Establishes the standalone math is bit-identical to the deployed contract.
Standalone denormImpl == real _denormalizeAmount bytecode for dec6 over symbolic (amount, rate).
claimerPayment >= 10**(18-6)  =>  actualPayment > 0 (dec6, 1:1). Upper half of the exact zero-payment boundary.
0 < claimerPayment < 10**(18-6)  =>  actualPayment == 0 (dec6, 1:1). Lower half of the exact zero-payment boundary.
For an 18-dec, 1:1 reward token, claimerPayment > 0 => actualPayment > 0. An 18-dec reward token is immune to the decimal floor; the hazard requires a sub-18-dec reward token (e.g. USDC).
denormalize(normalize(x,18,1e18)) == x exactly (lossless) for an 18-dec, 1:1 token.
normalize(denormalize(y,6,1e18)) <= y for y < 1e15. The denormalize step never over-charges (floor-only); refutes any over-production.

inconclusive_timeouts: check_roundTrip_dec6 / _dec8 / _dec18 (symbolic rate): denormalize(normalize(x)) <= x — solver timeout on (x*scale*rate)/.../scale udiv. Property holds by manual proof (each step floors).

check_roundTrip_exact_noRate_dec6 / check_roundTrip_dec6_rate1_bounded: (x*1e12)/1e12 == x (and <= x). Mathematically exact (x*1e12 divisible by 1e12, x<1e30 no overflow) but the mul-then-div inversion is intractable for yices/z3 at 256-bit. The complementary no-overcharge direction (div-then-mul) WAS proven (check_noOvercharge_dec6_rate1_bounded PASS).
check_noOvercharge_dec6/8/18 (symbolic rate) and check_noOvercharge_dec6_rateDepeg_bounded / check_roundTrip_dec*_rateDepeg_bounded: nonlinear symbolic-rate division timeout.

manualProofSupplement.roundTrip: denormalize(normalize(x)) <= x: normalize multiplies/scales-with-floor, denormalize divides-with-floor; floor(floor(x*A*r/1e18)*1e18/r / B) <= x because each floor only decreases the value and the scale factors A=10**(18-d), B=10**(18-d) cancel. When rate==1e18 (no adjustment) the round-trip is LOSSLESS (x*A divisible by A). Halmos proved the lossless case for d=18 and the no-overcharge direction for d=6.
manualProofSupplement.noOvercharge: normalize(denormalize(y)) <= y by the same floor-monotonicity; proven in-domain by Halmos.
manualProofSupplement.deadCode: decimals>18 branches in _normalizeAmount (L599-601) and _denormalizeAmount (L635-636) are unreachable because setTokenConfig enforces decimals<=18 (InvalidDecimals). The SLITHER-001 divide-before-multiply is confined to that dead denormalize branch.
